record.intervention: Proteasome-inhibitor anticancer therapy; the public protocol does not name the study drug.
record.special_requirement: The study team must confirm a B-cell lymphoid neoplasm by histopathology, cytology and PCR clonality; the animal must maintain normal daily activities, attend visits, and have no change to prior treatment during the week before study start.
record.notes: Single-center trial for dogs and cats with B-cell lymphoid tumors. The current recruitment index and individual protocol were both read on 2026-10-09. Named disease scope includes lymphoma, plasmacytoma/multiple myeloma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia; B-cell confirmation controls eligibility. The study describes proteasome inhibitors used in human hematologic cancer and cites a feline bortezomib case as background, but does not explicitly name its study drug. Do not assume all lymphoma subtypes or a chemotherapy-naive requirement. Prior treatment must be unchanged for one week before starting; visit schedule and full medical eligibility require investigator confirmation. Costs are not publicly specified.

record.title: Oral targeted therapy for mutation-positive canine lung cancer
record.intervention: Oral molecularly targeted anticancer drug selected for a qualifying tumor mutation; the public protocol does not name the drug or mutation.
record.special_requirement: Nihon University must confirm a qualifying tumor mutation and that lung-tumor surgery is unsuitable or declined. Dogs with no remaining lesion after surgery cannot enroll; visits are weekly for three weeks.
record.notes: Single-center treatment trial for dogs with lung cancer who are not surgical candidates or whose owners decline surgery. The official current index and full primary protocol were read on 2026-10-09. Requires weight at least 4 kg, mutation-positive tumor testing at Nihon University, and ability to maintain eating, elimination and other normal daily activities. Dogs with no lesion after surgery are excluded. The oral drug is approved for human lung cancer but is not named on the public veterinary protocol; efficacy and adverse effects are evaluated over three weeks with weekly visits. No requirement for absence of previous chemotherapy or metastasis was published, so neither is inferred. Full eligibility and all costs require study-team confirmation.
